newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European shares sharply down on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European shares sharply down on rate worries.

text.p: European bourses slipped sharply on Thursday, weighed down by another fall on Wall Street and concerns about interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic.
And the dollar was steady around its session lows against the mark and yen at midday with activity thin ahead of key events later in the day.
The U.S. currency shrugged off the Bundesbank's decision to keep rates steady, as expected, but dealers said a growing sentiment for higher German rates persisted.

"The rate outlook has been changing for Germany to a tightening bias, with the view now that the pessimism of a German recovery has been overdone," said a Japanese bank dealer. "But people aren't expecting any Buba action for a while yet."

Another focus was U.S. trade data due at 1330 GMT. Analysts said the numbers would be under closer scrutiny after the widening Japanese trade surplus with the United States announced earlier in the week week.

The markets were also looking for some lead from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, who was due to speak in Washington at 1500 GMT against a background of figures on Wedneday showing U.S. consumer prices rose more than expected last month.

With a growing conviction in world markets that the Federal Reserve will raise rates on March 25 in a pre-emptive strike against inflationary pressures, Greenspan's words will be closely scrutinised for clues.
Interest rate concerns and the 19-point fall in the Dow overnight spooked bourses in Europe.

London, the continent's biggest exchange, was down three-quarters of a percent at noon GMT, slightly off its lows. Paris was off around one percent, up from a 1.5 percent deficit earlier on the morning and Frankfurt was down about one-and-a-quarter percent.
London dealers said concerns about interest rates and politics were depressing the market and keeping buyers at bay.

Lower-than-expected British retail price inflation figures and a batch of encouraging corporate results failed to lift the gloomy tone, and dealers said that although selling pressure was limited, the market was left vulnerable by a dearth of buyers.
"There's not much selling, but although we've seen some good results today, at the moment people are concerned about the economy and the political outlook," one dealer said.
The market was overhung with concerns that interest rates would rise soon after Britain's May 1 general election.

"In the short term, because of the election and the interest rate situation, the trend in the market is downwards," the head of UK equity sales at one brokerage said. "Interest rates ought to go up now and whoever wins the election is going to have to put them up. The only question is how much."

A batch of corporate results, including full-year figures from drinks giant Guinness Plc, provided some support to the London market. Guinness shares gained 7-1/2p to 493-1/2, and were the most heavily traded stock of the day.
In Frankfurt, German shares were dragged lower by the impact of a falling equity futures market combined with the weak sentiment emerging from the United States.
Dealers blamed lower U.S. Treasuries and the fall in the Dow overnight for the weakness. "All in all, there is a lot of pressure on the market today," one said.
The main market focus was the restarting of trade in Thyssen and Krupp-Hoesch after two days of suspension related to Krupp's attempt to produce a merger of their steel businesses.
In Paris it was a similar story and the blue chip CAC-40 index took a steep slide. Traders said profit-taking was partly to blame as Thursday was the last day of the month's trading account.
They said the markets were similarly cautious over possible U.S. interest rate tightening and sharp falls in bond markets.
CURRENCIES AT NOON GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6760 marks and 122.66 yen, compared with Wednesday's late European levels of 1.6808 and 122.59.
STOCK MARKETS AT NOON GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 29.5 points at 4,302.6.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 33.23 at 3,282.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 24.21 points at 2,572.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $352.70 versus London's close of $348.95 on Wednesday. Silver was four cents firmer at $5.25.
